Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 43, "heading": "CHAPTER 41. DORA’S AUNTS", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u043-b0030", "target": "Его честное лицо, когда он смотрел на меня, полушутливо-полусерьёзно качая головой, запечатлелось в моей памяти ярче, чем тогда, в действительности: к этому времени я был в таком состоянии крайнего трепета и рассеянности, что совершенно не мог сосредоточить внимание ни на чём. Когда мы подходили к дому, где жили мисс Спенлоу, я так упал в цене и по своему виду, и по присутствию духа, что Трэдлс предложил слабое возбуждающее в виде кружки эля. Приняв это средство в соседнем трактире, он повёл меня нетвёрдыми шагами к двери мисс Спенлоу.", "source_sha256": "07b09dcb1d4a35b48df7e1dd673b5cd55645927a05ca3c570cb0a1a7762c3247", "target_id": "ru-en85-u043-b0030", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "9471d1ec42bec783eac5dd52da414022a939f34246904cac888b75339a98da90"}, {"source_id": "en85-u043-b0031", "target": "Когда горничная открыла её, у меня было смутное ощущение, будто я как бы выставлен напоказ, и будто я каким-то образом колеблющейся походкой пересекаю прихожую с барометром и вхожу в тихую маленькую гостиную в нижнем этаже с видом на опрятный сад. Ещё помню, как сел там на диван и увидел, что волосы Трэдлса, теперь, когда он снял шляпу, вскочили, подобно тем назойливым фигуркам на пружинах, что выпрыгивают из ненастоящих табакерок, когда снимаешь крышку. Помню также, как слушал старомодные часы, тикавшие на каминной полке, и пытался заставить их идти в такт подскокам моего сердца, — чего они не желали. Помню, как оглядывал комнату в поисках хоть какого-нибудь признака Доры и не находил ни одного. Как мне показалось, что Джип где-то вдалеке один раз тявкнул и тут же был кем-то задушен. В конце концов я обнаружил, что пячу Трэдлса к камину и в величайшем смущении кланяюсь двум сухоньким пожилым дамам в чёрном, каждая из которых удивительно походила на изваяние из щепы или дубильной коры покойного мистера Спенлоу.", "source_sha256": "fce5e996db589c021446d888d9ad8910b93e096c46f379463e5fe7d42ddea9a9", "target_id": "ru-en85-u043-b0031", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "7fd700d2ad9582ff35d61f0750f68f26bc3af3f424a7e27f67860c43aa1e66e5"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 41, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u043-b0032", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Pray,’ said one of the two little ladies, ‘be seated.’", "sha256": "9a05f20e8f0cdd4a10c2634d2ba141a20034c7838c8612f6637edef1a79c7132", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[32]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0033", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "When I had done tumbling over Traddles, and had sat upon something which was not a cat—my first seat was—I so far recovered my sight, as to perceive that Mr. Spenlow had evidently been the youngest of the family; that there was a disparity of six or eight years between the two sisters; and that the younger appeared to be the manager of the conference, inasmuch as she had my letter in her hand—so familiar as it looked to me, and yet so odd!—and was referring to it through an eye-glass. They were dressed alike, but this sister wore her dress with a more youthful air than the other; and perhaps had a trifle more frill, or tucker, or brooch, or bracelet, or some little thing of that kind, which made her look more lively. They were both upright in their carriage, formal, precise, composed, and quiet. The sister who had not my letter, had her arms crossed on her breast, and resting on each other, like an Idol.", "sha256": "7c83613acf57191e0c9264463c224413c21d470de9486300a17ac44d425f183d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[33]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0034", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mr. Copperfield, I believe,’ said the sister who had got my letter, addressing herself to Traddles.", "sha256": "d0cbe998bdff466e91fcfd56e51e8be89fe2c6833a2e3a6d1e4483862d80501d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[34]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0035", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "This was a frightful beginning. Traddles had to indicate that I was Mr. Copperfield, and I had to lay claim to myself, and they had to divest themselves of a preconceived opinion that Traddles was Mr. Copperfield, and altogether we were in a nice condition. To improve it, we all distinctly heard Jip give two short barks, and receive another choke.", "sha256": "a1f359becf40e89ea4a959809d42c60136bec38c58b45b2d33924bc6dd39286d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[35]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0036", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mr. Copperfield!’ said the sister with the letter.", "sha256": "e5e32b9fd98562ceb55d8447d1866dfe2e08672f5a58c2dab681471c8d644cf9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[36]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0037", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I did something—bowed, I suppose—and was all attention, when the other sister struck in.", "sha256": "9e307445a8546fb7de39779f2627eb014d46a03291f6fe3fe683a18161225e56", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[37]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0038", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My sister Lavinia,’ said she ‘being conversant with matters of this nature, will state what we consider most calculated to promote the happiness of both parties.’", "sha256": "3798b8a60ad36cd4dcc438eceb9c6926e7b996054447412cd67cdd270248a6a3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[39]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0039", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I discovered afterwards that Miss Lavinia was an authority in affairs of the heart, by reason of there having anciently existed a certain Mr. Pidger, who played short whist, and was supposed to have been enamoured of her. My private opinion is, that this was entirely a gratuitous assumption, and that Pidger was altogether innocent of any such sentiments—to which he had never given any sort of expression that I could ever hear of. Both Miss Lavinia and Miss Clarissa had a superstition, however, that he would have declared his passion, if he had not been cut short in his youth (at about sixty) by over-drinking his constitution, and over-doing an attempt to set it right again by swilling Bath water. They had a lurking suspicion even, that he died of secret love; though I must say there was a picture of him in the house with a damask nose, which concealment did not appear to have ever preyed upon.", "sha256": "e6a0c0838336e624b0a07e2a470292781613fb754ad3e92f0dfa343bd11d668c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[40]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0040", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘We will not,’ said Miss Lavinia, ‘enter on the past history of this matter. Our poor brother Francis’s death has cancelled that.’", "sha256": "0c96d590f1b085b706a8bd89c46d858e26bc382391d677f03881f9e5eeaaaea7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[41]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0041", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘We had not,’ said Miss Clarissa, ‘been in the habit of frequent association with our brother Francis; but there was no decided division or disunion between us. Francis took his road; we took ours. We considered it conducive to the happiness of all parties that it should be so. And it was so.’", "sha256": "ad969ff2bcfa7e65ba8f2d936d23e68cceb2214120d39223a543d2183135f272", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[42]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0042", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Each of the sisters leaned a little forward to speak, shook her head after speaking, and became upright again when silent. Miss Clarissa never moved her arms. She sometimes played tunes upon them with her fingers—minuets and marches I should think—but never moved them.", "sha256": "b7da712e4a7acb8d7ab28746bd376785eb4436e4f65db775013e3020ee727906", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[43]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0043", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Our niece’s position, or supposed position, is much changed by our brother Francis’s death,’ said Miss Lavinia; ‘and therefore we consider our brother’s opinions as regarded her position as being changed too. We have no reason to doubt, Mr. Copperfield, that you are a young gentleman possessed of good qualities and honourable character; or that you have an affection—or are fully persuaded that you have an affection—for our niece.’", "sha256": "e16317341a6b861ed0157c44ae96571d27e5fa675042714969a18ccffcb1f34f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[44]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0044", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I replied, as I usually did whenever I had a chance, that nobody had ever loved anybody else as I loved Dora. Traddles came to my assistance with a confirmatory murmur.", "sha256": "8d58f6bc5b6f36bd518dbc4d8511f7a1a6aea90ee04f48cab3e45a75b6bac465", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[45]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0045", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Miss Lavinia was going on to make some rejoinder, when Miss Clarissa, who appeared to be incessantly beset by a desire to refer to her brother Francis, struck in again:", "sha256": "4823f3ba504bd550193287e07fc245554d79814e56fa95bac291fb5652798d76", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[46]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0046", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘If Dora’s mama,’ she said, ‘when she married our brother Francis, had at once said that there was not room for the family at the dinner-table, it would have been better for the happiness of all parties.’", "sha256": "ed8c00904eee02e1c1f9e6a93cfebc62474cac79f69b0647fefbaada7cf24b29", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[47]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0047", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Sister Clarissa,’ said Miss Lavinia. ‘Perhaps we needn’t mind that now.’", "sha256": "676789c930ad42f45bffd2eb11d9db2285efe973c5ce14219b4b5b5b068cf67a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[48]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0048", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Sister Lavinia,’ said Miss Clarissa, ‘it belongs to the subject. With your branch of the subject, on which alone you are competent to speak, I should not think of interfering. On this branch of the subject I have a voice and an opinion. It would have been better for the happiness of all parties, if Dora’s mama, when she married our brother Francis, had mentioned plainly what her intentions were. We should then have known what we had to expect. We should have said “Pray do not invite us, at any time”; and all possibility of misunderstanding would have been avoided.’", "sha256": "6413834d11a543eb54db4182e5787a329f2801928b2eae91238d318c5f76fa19", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[49]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0049", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "When Miss Clarissa had shaken her head, Miss Lavinia resumed: again referring to my letter through her eye-glass. They both had little bright round twinkling eyes, by the way, which were like birds’ eyes. They were not unlike birds, altogether; having a sharp, brisk, sudden manner, and a little short, spruce way of adjusting themselves, like canaries.", "sha256": "b854d73d9c60cef6174d6e307d4e84e40073f006fb0a9d35dc0f16cf644a1cfc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[50]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0050", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Miss Lavinia, as I have said, resumed:", "sha256": "d118622f69fc40c3fbc76a0d91d434871831b30e9534634691446266b5bc85fc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[51]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0051", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You ask permission of my sister Clarissa and myself, Mr. Copperfield, to visit here, as the accepted suitor of our niece.’", "sha256": "8c69833c899dc8b9418922f7403794a83e4b8894473a14ff54de1be42d01b223", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[52]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0052", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘If our brother Francis,’ said Miss Clarissa, breaking out again, if I may call anything so calm a breaking out, ‘wished to surround himself with an atmosphere of Doctors’ Commons, and of Doctors’ Commons only, what right or desire had we to object? None, I am sure. We have ever been far from wishing to obtrude ourselves on anyone. But why not say so? Let our brother Francis and his wife have their society. Let my sister Lavinia and myself have our society. We can find it for ourselves, I hope.’", "sha256": "712d66888b4fc86abc5117ecb05717beec4770d9a80310211cd98899fda79168", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[53]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0053", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "As this appeared to be addressed to Traddles and me, both Traddles and I made some sort of reply. Traddles was inaudible. I think I observed, myself, that it was highly creditable to all concerned. I don’t in the least know what I meant.", "sha256": "34f088797cd7ddc38f425b1b6d6b6eff74a74a22a093ce7dda52fe6d9190d62b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[54]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0054", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Sister Lavinia,’ said Miss Clarissa, having now relieved her mind, ‘you can go on, my dear.’", "sha256": "4b66e61a4c6e708fba1d04ac529533b8bd4ad07b0d51ca367c0adef803ceb12f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[55]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0055", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Miss Lavinia proceeded:", "sha256": "f390d3180824854889e9b1d09ec2c406060187b89f86ec546c454723589b1786", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[56]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0056", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mr. Copperfield, my sister Clarissa and I have been very careful indeed in considering this letter; and we have not considered it without finally showing it to our niece, and discussing it with our niece. We have no doubt that you think you like her very much.’", "sha256": "34f29f6359515cfa46341d6282a3b52fc7181658a7f4ebfe2ac5021372e457c2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[57]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0057", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Think, ma’am,’ I rapturously began, ‘oh!—’", "sha256": "77e00fd928bdb52e3eddc689978ecb7151a0cfac7dc584999bed3ae09156da31", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[58]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0058", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But Miss Clarissa giving me a look (just like a sharp canary), as requesting that I would not interrupt the oracle, I begged pardon.", "sha256": "2acacba31526f5d612d4862887a9ce65cc4d511e5bfb26dff6575556bee3c716", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[59]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0059", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Affection,’ said Miss Lavinia, glancing at her sister for corroboration, which she gave in the form of a little nod to every clause, ‘mature affection, homage, devotion, does not easily express itself. Its voice is low. It is modest and retiring, it lies in ambush, waits and waits. Such is the mature fruit. Sometimes a life glides away, and finds it still ripening in the shade.’", "sha256": "2a38818092b19962509966c01170c9a67d66567b0cbc0d6803522e7ec5058b5c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[60]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0060", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of course I did not understand then that this was an allusion to her supposed experience of the stricken Pidger; but I saw, from the gravity with which Miss Clarissa nodded her head, that great weight was attached to these words.", "sha256": "679d6c18a79ddf77499264ff434de84b6c51997e9bff5b75aa9c4213810f0556", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[61]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0061", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘The light—for I call them, in comparison with such sentiments, the light—inclinations of very young people,’ pursued Miss Lavinia, ‘are dust, compared to rocks. It is owing to the difficulty of knowing whether they are likely to endure or have any real foundation, that my sister Clarissa and myself have been very undecided how to act, Mr. Copperfield, and Mr.—’", "sha256": "33554f7d3fb7885e29ea2f68e4c3ce2925e465f9694fa83add39bcf5f8b0da35", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[62]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0062", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Traddles,’ said my friend, finding himself looked at.", "sha256": "99caba3c3384495da4512950bde617123c2b7e8c6f5f5287d774432bdc2110de", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[63]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0063", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I beg pardon.
